sentences.text: Researchers examined how social isolation affects alcohol consumption and aversion-resistant drinking in male and female Wistar rats using behavioral tests such as two-bottle choice and quinine-adulterated drinking.

Isolation during early adolescence or continuous isolation increased alcohol intake in both sexes compared to controls, whereas isolation restricted to late adolescence did not significantly alter drinking behavior.

While male rats showed similar increases in alcohol drinking regardless of the isolation timing, only continuous isolation led to higher aversion-resistant drinking in female rats at the highest quinine concentration and increased intake after abstinence.

The findings suggest that early adolescent isolation leads to lasting increases in alcohol-related behaviors, although re-socialization may offer some protection for females against specific drinking patterns.
